categories.name: Overall aesthetic
categories.summary: Found internet footage is the film; graphics are thin proof around it. Dark grounds, vignettes, VHS damage and red accents make every built shot look recovered from a hard drive, not designed.

rules.title: Raw is the base
rules.text: Raw found footage is the base: 42-92% of runtime, median 72% across 15 videos. Graphics median 28%; only v10 is graphics-majority (58%).

rules.title: Graphics have a job
rules.text: Every graphic does one job: prove (page), date (card), locate (map) or point (callout). No decorative graphic.

rules.title: Many short graphic clips
rules.text: Many clips, few seconds: 34-126 clips per video (1144 over 15). Motion-graphic clips average about 7.8 s (est., range 4.7-13.1 s per video).

rules.title: Dark ground
rules.text: Built shots sit on dark ground: black, a dimmed or blurred copy of the footage, or a dark page, always with a vignette (est.).

evidence.label: v12 · Group photo, blurred bg push

rules.title: Analog damage
rules.text: Analog damage is the house texture: VHS grain and scan lines on cards, static bursts, RGB tears, PLAY tags, pixel fonts. RGB tear in 12 of 15 videos, static in 5.

rules.title: Native aspect
rules.text: Raw clips keep their native aspect (9:16 phone, 4:3 tape) on a blurred enlarged copy or dark pillarbox with vignette (6 of 15).

rules.title: Keep source overlays
rules.text: The source's own overlays stay: bodycam timestamps, CCTV labels, stream chat, LIVE tags, burned camera dates (est.).

rules.title: Same blocks, new arrangement
rules.text: Each video picks its own look for cards and captions (pixel font, serif or bold sans); the building blocks repeat, the intro never does. No two of 15 intros share a structure.

categories.name: Mood and emotion
categories.summary: Cold dread from real footage. The edit lets the clip scare, then proves it is real; damage effects and colour drains mark the moments where something goes wrong.

rules.title: Cold open
rules.text: Open cold on the strongest raw moment: first frame is raw footage in 11 of 15 videos; no logo or title at 0:00 in any.

evidence.label: v13 · Cold open at the door

rules.title: Loud intro
rules.text: The intro hits harder: intro loudness is usually 1-3 dB above the whole video (v05 -10.6 vs -13.2 LUFS; v06 -10.9 vs -13.2).

rules.title: Facts, no jokes
rules.text: Tone is documentary, not jokey: graphics state facts (date, place, name, source) and never comment on the scare (est.).

rules.title: Colour drain before disaster
rules.text: Drain colour to black and white with a vignette, or show a camcorder STOP icon, at the moment before a disaster or death (6 of 15).

rules.title: Quiet human close
rules.text: Close a death or loss on a quiet human photo with a colour drain or fade, not a graphic (3 of 15: v08, v11, v12).

evidence.label: v11 · Brittany photo, fade to grey

rules.title: Tease the next case
rules.text: Keep tension across cases: 5-30 s of the next case's footage plays before the dip to black (5 of 15).

evidence.label: v01 · Next-case preview in red frame

rules.title: Damage at the scare
rules.text: Make the recovered footage feel uncanny with damage at the scare: RGB tear (8-13 frames) or static burst (0.1-1 s), not a jump-scare sting on every cut.

categories.name: Color palette
categories.summary: Near-black grounds with white text and red as the one strong accent. Highlights add yellow or blue; subtitles are colour-coded by speaker. Footage keeps its own colour unless it drains to black and white.

rules.title: Red accent
rules.text: Red is the accent: frames, arrows, circles, node lines, highlight bars, the logo and the red last word or second line of a title.

evidence.label: v13 · Red frame to clip wall

rules.title: White on dark
rules.text: Text is white on dark: date cards, name tags, time-jump titles and quote cards.

rules.title: Highlight colours
rules.text: Highlight the line the voice reads with a yellow, red or blue sweep (12 of 15).

rules.title: Speaker colours
rules.text: Subtitles on raw are coloured by speaker: white, blue, yellow; red for sounds or an unseen voice (12 of 15 burn subtitles).

rules.title: Call colours
rules.text: 911 call waveform: red glow, white caller lines, blue or cyan operator lines (4 of 15).

rules.title: Page tint
rules.text: Pages may take a colour tint on entry (v04 Reddit pages: green-pink-red tint).

rules.title: Dark red ground
rules.text: Time-jump and quote cards can sit on a dark red vignette (v05 '2 Years Earlier...').

rules.title: VCR blue
rules.text: VCR PLAY card is the blue VCR screen with white PLAY, SP and timecode (v10).

rules.title: Leave raw colour
rules.text: Raw colour is not graded to a house look; it changes only for a black-and-white drain or a VHS grade on a zoom (est.).

evidence.label: v01 · Zoom on woman, VHS grade

categories.name: Lighting
categories.summary: There is no lighting to set: the footage is what it is, mostly night, torch, night-vision and CCTV. The edit controls light only on built shots, with vignettes, glow and dimming.

rules.title: Dark sources stay dark
rules.text: Source footage is mostly dark: night torch, infrared night vision, CCTV, doorbell cams. It is not brightened (est.).

evidence.label: v13 · Cold open at the door

rules.title: Dim under text
rules.text: Dim or blur the footage before text goes on it (quote or text on dimmed footage in 7 of 15).

evidence.label: v11 · Typed quote on dim stream

rules.title: Text glow
rules.text: Titles, dates and the logo glow softly (glow date cards in v04, v05, v15).

rules.title: Vignette
rules.text: Every built shot gets a vignette: dark edges, light centre (est.).

categories.name: Camera angles
categories.summary: Angles come from whoever filmed it: bodycam, CCTV corner, doorbell, selfie, stream cam. The edit adds only the views of pages and maps.

rules.title: Source angle
rules.text: Use the source angle as it is: bodycam, high CCTV corner, doorbell, selfie stream, first-person POV. No staged angles.

rules.title: Second angle as PIP
rules.text: When a second camera exists, show it as a PIP inset rather than cutting away (v01 bodycam inset, v07 corner inset).

evidence.label: v01 · Bodycam inset over witness footage

rules.title: Map views
rules.text: Maps are top-down satellite or tilted 3D aerial or tilt-shift; Street View for the street level.

rules.title: Page angle
rules.text: Pages are shown on a 3D tilt or flat with blur and vignette, never as a plain full-screen screenshot (est.).

categories.name: Camera movement
categories.summary: Raw footage keeps its own handheld motion. Every built shot moves a little: slow push on pages, photos and maps; punch-ins and strobe cuts point at one detail.

rules.title: Raw motion only
rules.text: Raw keeps its own motion; whip and zoom blur appear only inside raw footage, not as added transitions.

rules.title: Slow push
rules.text: Pages, photos and maps never sit still: slow push or slow drift (est.).

evidence.label: v12 · Group photo, blurred bg push

rules.title: Punch-in
rules.text: Punch-in zoom on one detail, 1-4 s (5 of 15).

rules.title: Strobe on words
rules.text: Strobe or word-synced cuts: 2-10 frame flashes, about one per narrated word (v04); repeated push per word held 3-5 frames (v06).

rules.title: Grid move
rules.text: Grids and walls move: shrink, pan, then zoom into the chosen cell.

evidence.label: v13 · Red frame to clip wall
v11 · Case grid, pan to Case 2

rules.title: Map move
rules.text: Maps fly in Google-Earth style or drift over a tilt-shift aerial, 3-15 s.

evidence.label: v14 · Google Earth runway, red arrow

categories.name: Shot composition
categories.summary: Subject centred; everything that is not the footage is small and kept out of its way. Pages float on blurred backgrounds; vertical clips sit on their own blurred copy.

rules.title: Caption position
rules.text: Captions sit bottom centre, about y 91% of frame, about 27 px tall on 720p, one line (v03, v04).

rules.title: Name tag position
rules.text: Name tags are small and placed on the person: on the chest, beside the head, or under a small framed portrait.

rules.title: Corner furniture
rules.text: Channel pop-up sits top-centre; corner date stamp bottom-left; PLAY tag top-left; PIP in a corner.

evidence.label: v02 · Vlog frame, date, channel pop-up

rules.title: Page placement
rules.text: Pages are centred or tilted with a blurred, vignetted background.

rules.title: Blurred copy fill
rules.text: Vertical or 4:3 footage and photos sit on a blurred enlarged copy of themselves, not black bars (6 of 15).

rules.title: Callout on target
rules.text: Callouts sit on the detail itself (arrow onto the sleeper, circle round the knife), never in a separate panel.

evidence.label: v13 · Woman with knife, red tag

rules.title: Grid layout
rules.text: Grids hold 4-10 cells, each in a thin red frame, numbered (v13 1-10, v14 1-6, v11 CASE 1-4).

categories.name: Editing rhythm
categories.summary: Long raw runs, short graphic bridges. Scene detection gives a median of 12 s per cut over the whole video and 8.2 s in the intro; raw clips run 10-60 s while pages and cards take 2-10 s.

rules.title: Shot length
rules.text: Average shot per detected cut: median 12 s (6.6 s v10 to 19.2 s v06); intro median 8.2 s; after 90 s median 14 s. Detection undercounts.

rules.title: Long raw runs
rules.text: Raw clips run 10-60 s (to 170 s in v07); captions change instead of cuts.

evidence.label: v07 · Live stream footage, tight light

rules.title: Short graphics
rules.text: Graphic and page stretches run 2-4 s per shot; a graphic lasts 2-10 s.

rules.title: Proof breaks
rules.text: Inside a long raw run, a page or comments break comes every 30-60 s.

rules.title: Headline flashes
rules.text: Headline flash run on a spoken list: 3-4 pages at 0.7-1.2 s each (v02, v11).

rules.title: Intro cut rate
rules.text: Intro cut rate in the first 90 s: median 20 cuts at scene threshold 0.2 (range 3 in v06 to 125 in v09 flicker).

rules.title: Glitch rate
rules.text: Glitch accents roughly once per 20-60 s (est.), never on every cut.

rules.title: Callback clip
rules.text: Return to the key clip whenever the story circles back (v05 CCTV clip returns 3 times; v15 same red label each return).

evidence.label: v05 · CCTV replay of the clip

rules.title: Narrated pace
rules.text: Ease into a narrated story faster: v05 intro ran one cut per 2.6 s (graphics and B-roll), later narration about 14 s per cut (est.).

categories.name: Transitions
categories.summary: Hard cuts do the work (about 85-90% of joins). Pages dissolve in and out, cases are split by a dip to black, and short RGB tears or static bursts cover graphic edges and scares.

rules.title: Hard cut default
rules.text: Hard cut for about 85-90% of all joins (est.).

rules.title: Page dissolve
rules.text: Dissolve pages and cards in and out over 10-16 frames (0.3-0.5 s); never hard cut to a page (12 of 15).

evidence.label: v04 · YouTube page of Phil's video

rules.title: RGB tear
rules.text: RGB tear 8-13 frames on a cut or graphic edge (12 of 15).

rules.title: Black dip
rules.text: Dip to black between cases, 0.3-1.5 s (13 of 15). No wipes.

rules.title: Static burst
rules.text: VHS static burst 0.1-1 s into a tape, card or new case (5 of 15).

rules.title: Flash rare
rules.text: White flash is rare (v07, v10); keep it for one reveal at most (est.).

rules.title: Fade out
rules.text: End the video with a fade to black on the last frame (8 of 15).

rules.title: One-off bridges
rules.text: Special bridges are one-offs: film-strip montage (v10, about 12 s), glass shatter into a crime (v15).

categories.name: Typography
categories.summary: Small, quiet type: white serif, VCR mono or pixel font, bold sans for a few dates. Exact fonts are not verified; one family per video. Red marks the second line or last word.

rules.title: Date card type
rules.text: Date cards use one of three looks: VCR pixel or mono on grain (v03, v04, v07), small white serif (v06, v09, v10), or bold sans typed word by word (v13, v14).

rules.title: Name tag type
rules.text: Name tags: small serif or mono text, in a thin box or under a framed portrait.

rules.title: Caption chunks
rules.text: Captions follow phrases, 3-7 words, one line; they replace each other, no word-by-word pop.

rules.title: Caption style
rules.text: Caption style is set per video: uppercase VCR mono on a tight black box (v03, v04), small white sans with shadow (v01, v06, v09), larger white sans lower-case (v12, v13).

evidence.label: v13 · Cold open at the door

rules.title: Starred swears
rules.text: Star out profanity in captions ('F***').

rules.title: Audio tags
rules.text: Bad audio gets a short tag in place of a caption: '*Broken audio*'.

rules.title: Glow titles
rules.text: Titles glow: '2 Years Earlier...' in sentence case with an ellipsis, or uppercase '5 DAYS EARLIER'.

rules.title: Red second line
rules.text: Two-line titles put the second line or the last word in red ('THEIR FINAL MOMENTS').

rules.title: Type-on
rules.text: Text types on word by word or line by line for dates and quotes (v13, v14, v11).

categories.name: Music and sound
categories.summary: Loud, never silent. Median master -13.2 LUFS with the intro 1-3 dB hotter. A bed or room tone always runs; glitch zaps, static and impacts sit on the graphic hits. Music titles and exact SFX counts are not measured.

rules.title: Master loudness
rules.text: Master to about -13 LUFS integrated: median -13.2 (range -10.8 to -17.5); LRA median 8.6.

rules.title: Hot intro
rules.text: Intro 1-3 dB louder than the whole video.

rules.title: No silence
rules.text: No true silence: silencedetect (-45 dB, 0.7 s) found 0 gaps in 9 videos and 1-2 in 6. Quietest 50 ms level median -30 dBFS in intros.

rules.title: Bed level
rules.text: Under narration a music bed runs about 8-12 dB below the voice (est., v05). In raw compilations the bed is mostly ambience plus an occasional drone.

rules.title: No new cue per case
rules.text: A case starts with a card and a dip, not a new music piece (est.).

rules.title: SFX on hits
rules.text: SFX sit on graphic hits: glitch zaps on RGB cuts, static bursts, impacts on logo and cards, risers into cards (est.). Real designed hits about 4-10 per minute (est.).

rules.title: Dip before card
rules.text: A short near-silent dip (about 4 s in v04) before a date card resets the ear.

rules.title: Ticks
rules.text: Ticking under a narrated intro: about 12 even clock or heartbeat ticks in the first 9 s (v05).

rules.title: Keep raw audio
rules.text: Raw audio is kept under captions; the clip's own sound carries the scare (est.).

categories.name: Storytelling
categories.summary: Compilations of 4-6 cases, or one long story. Each case: dip to black, date, source page or map, then a long raw run with proof breaks; close on a proof page or the last footage. No outro card.

rules.title: Case count
rules.text: A compilation runs 4-6 cases; single-story videos (v05, v09) follow the same beats with one case.

rules.title: Case open
rules.text: Case open: dip to black, a date card within 3-5 s, then the source page or a map, then raw footage (9 of 15 this exact order).

rules.title: Source-first open
rules.text: Or open on the source: the YouTube watch page or post, often with the date on it (8 of 15).

rules.title: Locate
rules.text: When a place is named, show a map or aerial, 3-15 s (13 of 15).

rules.title: Name
rules.text: When a person is named, show a name tag at first appearance (9 of 15). In v08 a name tag opens every case.

rules.title: Prove
rules.text: Every claim gets its source page for 3-10 s, then back to footage.

rules.title: Case close
rules.text: Case close: end on a proof page or comments (10 of 15) or let the last raw play out with the outcome in narration (7 of 15).

rules.title: Grid teaser and recap
rules.text: A numbered grid works as the list teaser early and as the recap late (4 of 15).

rules.title: Bridge line
rules.text: Narration for case N+1 can start over its first footage while case N closes (v12, v13).

rules.title: Analysis beat
rules.text: Add outside voices for analysis: reaction creators, comments, explanation cards (v05, v07).

rules.title: No outro
rules.text: No outro card, subscribe screen or logo at the end of any of the 15 videos.

rulebook.title: Cold open
rulebook.text: No logo and no title at 0:00. Open on the strongest raw footage (11 of 15 start on raw; none shows a logo at 0:00).

evidence.label: v13 · Cold open at the door

rulebook.title: Date every case
rulebook.text: State the date before each case: a date card or date title within 3-5 s of the black dip (13 of 15 videos).

rulebook.title: Raw is the base
rulebook.text: Raw footage fills most of the runtime (median 72%, never under 42%). A graphic must prove, date, locate or point.

rulebook.title: Native aspect
rulebook.text: Raw clips keep their native aspect. Vertical or 4:3 goes on a blurred enlarged copy or dark pillarbox; never stretch or crop to fill.

rulebook.title: Caption raw speech
rulebook.text: Caption all raw speech (15 of 15): one line, 3-7 words, profanity starred.

rulebook.title: No silence
rulebook.text: Never true silence. A music bed or room tone always runs (0 gaps of -45 dB/0.7 s in 9 of 15 videos).

rulebook.title: Master loudness
rulebook.text: Master about -13 LUFS integrated (median -13.2); intro 1-3 dB louder than the rest.

rulebook.title: Censor
rulebook.text: Blur, pixelate or scribble over bodies, gore and private faces (11 of 15).

rulebook.title: Hard cuts
rulebook.text: About 85-90% of joins are hard cuts. Dissolves, tears and dips are accents with a job.

rulebook.title: No hard cut to a page
rulebook.text: Pages dissolve in and out over 10-16 frames (12 of 15).

rulebook.title: Show the source
rulebook.text: Every claim gets its source page on screen for 3-10 s, with the line the voice reads highlighted (pages 15 of 15, highlights 12 of 15).

rulebook.title: Black dip between cases
rulebook.text: Cases are split by a 0.3-1.5 s dip to black (13 of 15). No wipes.

rulebook.title: No outro
rulebook.text: No outro card, subscribe screen or end logo. End on proof or the last footage, then fade to black.

rulebook.title: Red means look here
rulebook.text: Callouts, frames, node lines and grids are red; red is the only strong accent colour.

rulebook.title: Short glitches
rulebook.text: RGB tears stay 8-13 frames and static bursts 0.1-1 s; never a glitch on every cut.

Generic rules: follow styleguide/_shared/GENERIC_RULES.md (shot length >= 3 s, audio cutting, SFX/music levels, loudness, transition hygiene, smoothness, QC, feedback loop). This guide's own rule book wins only where it says so explicitly.
rulebook.title: Generic rules

rulebook.text: Feedback loop: every owner note on a render goes into this guide the same day (rule book entry or rule, plus a Learnings entry, via model.apply_ops + model.save). The next build must read the rule book, the open Learnings and styleguide/_shared/GENERIC_RULES.md first; after each render check it against every line, fix what fails, then deliver.
rulebook.title: Feedback loop

graphics.title: VCR pixel date card
graphics.text: White pixel or VCR-mono date ('JULY 2022', 'NOVEMBER 2021 / THANKSGIVING WEEKEND') centred on dark VHS grain with faint scan lines. 3-4 s. Enters from black or static; one glitch band or a scan-line tear; exits by dissolve into the footage or into full static. Optional second line.
graphics.use: A case starts and the voice gives the month and year.
graphics.avoid: Inside a case; on a video whose other cards use serif.
graphics.why: Dates the case like a recovered tape label.

graphics.title: Glowing date and place card
graphics.text: Black, then two lines of glowing white text: date on top ('August 2nd, 2020'), place smaller below ('Guadalajara, Mexico'). 3-4 s, fades up, fades away.
graphics.use: The story clock starts and the place matters.
graphics.avoid: When a map will name the place straight after.
graphics.why: Sets time and place in one beat.

graphics.title: Typed date title over footage
graphics.text: Dip to black; bold white date types on word by word ('OCTOBER', '14TH,', '2025') with a red flash on each word or a red last word; the footage fades up behind it. 2-4 s.
graphics.use: Fast case starts in clip compilations (doorbell, final moments, live stream).
graphics.avoid: Slow narrated stories; use the glowing card there.
graphics.why: Gives the date without a separate card, so the clip starts sooner.

graphics.title: Small serif date over page or footage
graphics.text: Small white serif date ('September 2025', 'May 1989') fades in over a dim channel page, night exterior or tape, 2-5 s, then fades out. No box.

evidence.label: v01 · Date card on VHS footage

graphics.use: Dating a source page or old tape while it plays.
graphics.avoid: When the footage behind is bright; dim it first.
graphics.why: Quiet, keeps the source on screen.

graphics.title: Corner date stamp
graphics.text: Tiny white date text ('September 10th 2019') fades in at lower left of a framed video or page, 2-3 s (est.), then fades out.

evidence.label: v02 · Vlog frame, date, channel pop-up

graphics.use: The host's vlog or a page needs a date without stopping.
graphics.avoid: As the main case date; use a card.
graphics.why: Dates without covering the frame.

graphics.title: Time-jump title
graphics.text: Glowing white text '2 Years Earlier...', '3 Years Later', '1 DAY LATER', '5 DAYS EARLIER' over a dark red vignette, darkened aerial, page or clip. 2-4 s; fades in with a slight glow pulse or types in; fades out. 5 of 15 videos.
graphics.use: The story jumps back or forward in time.
graphics.avoid: For the first date of a case; use a date card.
graphics.why: Tells the viewer the clock moved.

graphics.title: Page tilt with highlight sweep
graphics.text: Article, post or site captured and shown on a 3D tilt (or flat) with vignette and blurred edges, slow push. 3-10 s (up to 16). A yellow, red or blue bar sweeps over the exact line the voice reads. Dissolve in and out 10-16 frames or RGB tear. 12 of 15 highlight.
graphics.use: The narration states a fact that a page backs up.
graphics.avoid: For a video that will play; use the YouTube watch page.
graphics.why: Proves the claim is on record and leads the eye to the line.
graphics.situation: Show the real page, post or document

graphics.title: Headline word boxes
graphics.text: Big headline on a dark page; white boxes appear behind the key words one by one as they are read; RGB tear or white flash on entry. 2-5 s.
graphics.use: Opening a case on a shocking headline.
graphics.avoid: Long article text; use the sweep bar.
graphics.why: Makes the headline read like a verdict.
graphics.situation: Stress a number, fact or outcome

graphics.title: Headline flash run
graphics.text: 3-4 pages or headlines cut in at 0.7-1.2 s each on a spoken list, then out. v02 and v11.
graphics.use: The voice lists reports or sources in one breath.
graphics.avoid: When one source matters; give it a full page tilt.
graphics.why: Shows how much coverage there was, fast.

graphics.title: YouTube watch page with footage playing
graphics.text: Dark YouTube watch page, footage playing in the player, sidebar blurred, slight push. 3-10 s. Glitch or dissolve in; the footage then expands to full frame. 8 of 15.
graphics.use: Start of a case or before the key clip, to show where it was posted.
graphics.avoid: When the source is not on YouTube; use the platform it was on.
graphics.why: The real upload proves the footage is real.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)

graphics.title: Stream page (Twitch, Kick, YouTube live)
graphics.text: The stream platform page, dimmed or zooming into the player; live chat on the side. Held still or slow zoom, then dissolve into full-frame stream footage.

evidence.label: v11 · Twitch page, game stream zoom
v11 · Twitch page zoom to stream

graphics.use: The footage was live-streamed.
graphics.avoid: For uploaded videos; use the watch page.
graphics.why: Shows it happened live, in public.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)

graphics.title: Channel pop-up pill
graphics.text: Dark rounded pill or card with avatar, channel name, subs and Subscribe, top-centre over the footage. Slides down or pops in, drifts up, leaves after 2-3 s. 3 of 15.

evidence.label: v02 · Vlog frame, date, channel pop-up

graphics.use: The voice names the creator who filmed it.
graphics.avoid: For people who are not channel owners; use a name tag.
graphics.why: Credits the source and shows a real account.

graphics.title: Channel page or video grid
graphics.text: The creator's channel page or grid of uploads, tilted or flat, slow scroll or push, 3-6 s; glitch in. 5 of 15.
graphics.use: Showing who the creator is or how much they posted.
graphics.avoid: When a pop-up says enough.
graphics.why: Gives the creator a life before the scare.

graphics.title: Social post in tilt
graphics.text: Facebook, Reddit, X or Instagram post on a 3D tilt with vignette; may take a green-pink-red tint (v04) or carry a red arrow; 3-16 s; RGB glitch at the end hands off to footage.

evidence.label: v06 · X post, tilt and highlight
v01 · Facebook post, New World Order image

graphics.use: The story starts from or turns on a post.
graphics.avoid: News facts; use an article page.
graphics.why: The post is the first-hand record.
graphics.situation: Show the real page, post or document

graphics.title: Comments page with red bar
graphics.text: Dark (or light) YouTube, Reddit or Facebook comments, zoomed, slow scroll or drift; a red marker swipe (or yellow) on the key line. 6-12 s (to 25). 11 of 15.

evidence.label: v01 · Reddit thread, zoom on comment

graphics.use: Reaction beat, doubt, or the case close.
graphics.avoid: As the first proof of a fact.
graphics.why: Shows how people reacted; a natural end to a case.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message

graphics.title: Comment ticker over footage
graphics.text: A comment, huge and blurred or small, slides across the live footage; one word flagged in a red box each time it appears. 3-6 s.
graphics.use: Viewers noticed something in the clip the viewer should look for.
graphics.avoid: When the footage needs full attention.
graphics.why: Brings the audience's reading into the clip.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message

graphics.title: Name tag on the person
graphics.text: Tiny white mono or serif text, sometimes in a thin box, placed on the chest or beside the head ('MOE SARGI', 'Steve Stephens'). Pops in, 1-4 s. 9 of 15.

evidence.label: v11 · Twitch channel page, name tag

graphics.use: A person is named or first seen.
graphics.avoid: When a portrait card is coming; do not tag twice.
graphics.why: The viewer knows who is on screen without a cutaway.

graphics.title: Framed portrait over blurred copy
graphics.text: Still photo in a thin frame, small serif name under it, over a dark blurred enlarged copy of the same face. Glitch or fade in and out, 3-9 s.
graphics.use: Naming a victim, suspect or family member with no footage of them.
graphics.avoid: When the person is on screen in raw; use the name tag.
graphics.why: Gives a face to a name with weight.

graphics.title: Glitch-face name tag
graphics.text: Black dip, then a black-and-white portrait with a mono name tag; the face breaks with glitch tears. 1-3 s. Opens every case in v08.
graphics.use: A case is about one person (final moments, missing creator).
graphics.avoid: Living bystanders.
graphics.why: Marks the person as lost before the story starts.

graphics.title: News lower third (kept from source)
graphics.text: The TV clip's own lower third stays on: white bar with black headline and red tag line ('BODY PULLED FROM BLACKSTONE RIVER'). 3-4 s. Not rebuilt.

evidence.label: v06 · TV news clip, school exterior

graphics.use: Using a local news clip as proof.
graphics.avoid: Do not build a fake news bar.
graphics.why: Real broadcast proof.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)

graphics.title: Red callout on footage
graphics.text: Red arrow, hand-drawn circle, box or bracket on the detail, often with a red uppercase or typed label ('VICTIMS SLEEPING', '*knife*'). Pops in without ease, 1-10 s; returns whenever the footage returns. 6 of 15.

evidence.label: v13 · Woman with knife, red tag
v11 · YouTube page, red box on walker

graphics.use: The scary detail is small or hard to see.
graphics.avoid: When the detail is already obvious.
graphics.why: Makes sure everyone sees it, without leaving the clip.

graphics.title: Typed label or quote on footage
graphics.text: Footage dims; a boxed label or quote types on ('Always had bad intentions', 'Is she AFK?'), sometimes with a red scan line sweep. 3-5 s. 7 of 15.

evidence.label: v11 · Typed quote on dim stream

graphics.use: Quoting chat, a message or a key line said off screen.
graphics.avoid: For speech the clip already has; caption it.
graphics.why: Puts the exact words on screen.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message

graphics.title: Glowing text card
graphics.text: Black or dimmed portrait; one white glowing line or short paragraph ('Work during the day... stay away from the shop at night'). About 3-5 s, fades in and out.

evidence.label: v15 · Lock your doors text card

graphics.use: A rule, statement or question is the beat.
graphics.avoid: Long text; use the page.
graphics.why: Lets one line land in silence.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message

graphics.title: Numbered red-frame grid
graphics.text: Footage gets a thin red border, shrinks and flies into a dark wall of numbered red-framed clips (1-6 or 1-10); camera pans and zooms into the next cell. 4-8 s. 4 of 15.

evidence.label: v13 · Red frame to clip wall

graphics.use: List video intro (table of contents) or recap.
graphics.avoid: Single-story videos.
graphics.why: Promises the list and shows progress.

graphics.title: Red-frame next-case teaser
graphics.text: Next case's footage plays small inside a red frame (or torn frames) on dark, 4-14 s, before the black dip.

evidence.label: v01 · Next-case preview in red frame
v01 · Next-case preview in red frame
v08 · Case preview in torn frames

graphics.use: Ending a case and hooking the next.
graphics.avoid: The last case.
graphics.why: Keeps the viewer through the case change.

graphics.title: Title over clip mosaic or film strip
graphics.text: After the cold open: a glitching mosaic of tiny clips or a curved 3D film strip, then white mono or glowing serif title with a red second line ('TIMES YOUTUBERS RECORDED / THEIR FINAL MOMENTS'). 2-4 s.

evidence.label: v10 · The Hidden Evils of Lost Media

graphics.use: Naming the video's theme once, after the hook (35-71 s in).
graphics.why: States the promise once the viewer is hooked.

graphics.title: Case title card
graphics.text: Dark grey flat card, plain small white serif 'Case 1', then the case name replaces it ('Interesting Hobby'). About 3 s each, about 6 s total. v10 only.
graphics.use: A list video with a fixed ritual per case.
graphics.avoid: Videos that date each case; the date card does the job.
graphics.why: Clean chapter mark.

graphics.title: Content warning card
graphics.text: Black to a dark card, red glowing 'Content Warning' header and three lines of tiny white text, about 3 s (v10). Lighter form: small red 'viewer discretion' label on the footage (v01).
graphics.use: Before graphic material.
graphics.avoid: As decoration; once per video.
graphics.why: Warns and builds dread.

graphics.title: VCR PLAY tag and card
graphics.text: Grey or white 'PLAY' camcorder label top-left on tape footage, or a blue VCR screen with PLAY, SP and a running timecode (00:00:00), 1-4 s, glitch out to black. 3 of 15 (plus a PLAY label in v06).
graphics.use: The clip is a home tape or a recovered recording.
graphics.avoid: Phone or stream footage.
graphics.why: Says 'this is a tape' in one second.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)

graphics.title: Black-and-white STOP / colour drain
graphics.text: Same clip turns black and white (nearly frozen) with a vignette or a camcorder STOP icon top-left. 2-4 s.

evidence.label: v11 · Brittany photo, fade to grey

graphics.use: The moment before a death or disaster.
graphics.avoid: Ordinary scares.
graphics.why: Freezes the last normal moment.
graphics.situation: Something breaks, goes wrong or feels uncanny

graphics.title: Tilt-shift aerial with label
graphics.text: Tilted 3D or tilt-shift aerial of the place, slow drift, soft edges; optional red circle and curved text label ('one of the best candy shops in the area'). 3-8 s; fade from black or crossfade.

evidence.label: v05 · Aerial map with text arc

graphics.use: A place is named.
graphics.avoid: When the exact route matters; use the satellite map.
graphics.why: Puts the scene somewhere real.
graphics.situation: Name a place or move to a new place

graphics.title: Aerial map with pin, photo or clip
graphics.text: Darkened aerial, slow drift; a framed photo or clip thumbnail pins onto the house, or a red pin and route draw on. 7-14 s.

evidence.label: v12 · Aerial map, pin and route
v10 · Aerial map with red pin

graphics.use: Opening or locating a case at a specific address.
graphics.avoid: A general region.
graphics.why: Links the footage to the spot.
graphics.situation: Name a place or move to a new place

graphics.title: Satellite map with labels and red arrow
graphics.text: Google-Earth style satellite push or fly-in, serif labels ('11 Days Earlier', '30 Minutes Later 5:27 PM'), red arrow animating along a path. 3-15 s.

evidence.label: v14 · Google Earth runway, red arrow
v14 · Satellite map, Kathmandu to Pokhara

graphics.use: Explaining distance, a route or timing.
graphics.avoid: When place alone matters.
graphics.why: Shows how it happened, not just where.
graphics.situation: Name a place or move to a new place

graphics.title: Street View sequence
graphics.text: Street View stills of the building, hard cuts between them (one per business or year), or Street View pulling up to the aerial; orange tint and vignette possible.

evidence.label: v14 · Location view of low wall

graphics.use: The history or look of one building.
graphics.avoid: Remote places.
graphics.why: Makes a real building familiar.
graphics.situation: Name a place or move to a new place

graphics.title: 911 call waveform
graphics.text: Slow aerial or dimmed footage; a red glowing audio waveform runs across, real call lines as white serif captions, operator in blue or cyan. About 10 s (to 40-50 s). 4 of 15.
graphics.use: Playing a real emergency call or last audio.
graphics.avoid: Audio that has its own video.
graphics.why: Makes audio watchable and real.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message

graphics.title: Recreated phone message
graphics.text: Dark phone screen; glowing blue iMessage bubble or voicemail with play bar and waveform, or a post typed line by line. Fades into the next shot.
graphics.use: The last message or a voicemail is part of the story.
graphics.avoid: When the real screenshot exists; show it as a page.
graphics.why: Personal, quiet, sad.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message

graphics.title: Photo card with slow push
graphics.text: Still on a dark or blurred-copy ground, soft shadow and vignette, slow push, cross-dissolve in and out. 3-9 s; couple photos 0.8-1 s each. 8 of 15.

evidence.label: v12 · Group photo, blurred bg push

graphics.use: Showing a person, place or object with no footage.
graphics.avoid: When footage exists.
graphics.why: Keeps stills alive.

graphics.title: Vertical clip on blurred copy
graphics.text: 9:16 or 4:3 footage centred on a blurred, darkened, enlarged copy of itself (or dark pillarbox), soft vignette. Whole clip length. 6 of 15.
graphics.use: Phone, doorbell or tape footage that is not 16:9.
graphics.avoid: Native 16:9 footage.
graphics.why: Keeps the source honest; no crop.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)

graphics.title: PIP inset
graphics.text: Second angle or portrait in a small dark-bordered or framed window in a corner over the main footage, 5-15 s.

evidence.label: v01 · Bodycam inset over witness footage
v12 · Webcam inset on blurred bg

graphics.use: Two cameras of one moment, or a victim present in archive footage.
graphics.avoid: When both need full size; use a split.
graphics.why: Shows both views at once.

graphics.title: Split compare and camera grid
graphics.text: Red-outlined frames side by side (before/after) or a 2x2 CCTV grid with red tracking squares, 5-10 s, with a caption ('Someone...').
graphics.use: Comparing two moments or several cameras.
graphics.avoid: Single-shot evidence.
graphics.why: Lets the viewer spot the change.

graphics.title: Hand-drawn or chalk board
graphics.text: Grey paper or dark chalk board; framed stills, handwriting and arrows appear step by step. 5-33 s. 3 of 15 (v06, v10, v11).
graphics.use: Explaining a plan, a deal, injuries or clues.
graphics.avoid: Simple facts.
graphics.why: Makes a complex link easy to follow.

graphics.title: Red node diagram
graphics.text: Dark red-tinted screen; framed screenshots or faces link up with red lines into a tree or web; pixel-build in, dissolve out. 4-8 s.

evidence.label: v11 · Joke diagram, red node tree

graphics.use: Showing who is linked to whom.
graphics.avoid: One person.
graphics.why: Shows the web of people.

graphics.title: RGB tear
graphics.text: RGB split with a horizontal scan-line break, 8-13 frames (as short as 3 frames), hard on the cut; glitch zap SFX.
graphics.use: Graphic edges, jump cuts inside a clip, scares.
graphics.avoid: Every cut.
graphics.why: Hides the cut and adds unease.

graphics.title: VHS static burst
graphics.text: Full-frame TV static, 0.1-1 s, sometimes two in a row; into a tape, card, or new case. Static noise SFX.
graphics.use: Entering a tape or a new case.
graphics.avoid: Inside a calm narration.
graphics.why: Sounds and looks like a tape changing.

graphics.title: Glass shatter bridge
graphics.text: Cracked-glass overlay builds over the shot in black and white shards, then fades off to the next angle. v15 only.
graphics.use: Into a violent crime.
graphics.avoid: More than once a video.
graphics.why: Breaks the calm.

graphics.title: NOCTURN logo sting
graphics.text: VHS static and red glitch blow in; glowing red NOCTURN condensed bold logo on black with a static bar, about 2 s, then 1 s static and glitch out to black. Once, about 49-62 s in (v05 only).
graphics.use: After the cold open of a narrated story.
graphics.avoid: At 0:00 or at the end.
graphics.why: Brands without delaying the hook.

graphics.title: Censor: blur, pixel, scribble
graphics.text: Soft Gaussian blur patch, mosaic pixel block, or a red scribble line over bodies, blood, faces or private screens; tracks the area. 11 of 15.
graphics.use: Bodies, gore, minors, private faces.
graphics.avoid: Faces that are the story and already public.
graphics.why: Stays watchable and within platform rules.

graphics.title: Burned-in subtitles
graphics.text: One-line phrase captions (3-7 words) bottom centre; style per video (VCR mono on black box, or white sans with shadow); coloured by speaker, red for sounds; short tags like '*Broken audio*'.

evidence.label: v13 · Cold open at the door

graphics.use: Any speech in raw footage.
graphics.avoid: Narration.
graphics.why: Raw audio is often unclear.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message

graphics.title: Punch-in and word strobe
graphics.text: Punch-in zoom on a detail 1-4 s, or repeated pushes/strobe cuts of 2-10 frames in time with each spoken word; zoom blur with a soft ring on the target.

evidence.label: v14 · Zoom blur, ring on ball

graphics.use: The voice names a detail in the clip.
graphics.avoid: Long holds.
graphics.why: Points without a graphic.

graphics.title: Stream overlay kept
graphics.text: Stream footage keeps its chat, LIVE tag, sub-goal bar, timer and gift pop-ups. 4 of 15.

evidence.label: v12 · Kick stream, then sleeping room
v07 · Live stream footage, tight light

graphics.use: The clip is from a live stream.
graphics.avoid: Do not fake an overlay.
graphics.why: Shows it happened live with viewers.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)

graphics_summary: Nocturn graphics are proof devices around raw footage: dates, source pages, maps, name tags and red callouts, each 2-10 s. Dark grounds, vignettes, white type and red accents; VHS static and RGB tears glue them to the footage. Pick by what the narration does; never add a graphic that does not prove, date, locate or point.

learnings.text: Owner 2026-11-12: every style guide follows the same generic craft rules learned from Farrell (audio cutting, clips >= 3 s, SFX and music levels, loudness, transition hygiene) so the video is smooth and human; they live in styleguide/_shared/GENERIC_RULES.md. Every guide keeps a feedback loop: owner notes enter the rule book and Learnings the same day and the next build reads them.
learnings.note: owner chat 2026-11-12: generic rules + feedback loop

meta.name: Nocturn
intro: Dark internet-horror compilation style, learned from 15 Nocturn videos (youtube.com/@Nocturn_real).
Follow it top to bottom on every Nocturn-style edit. The rule book comes first and is never skipped; then the categories; then pick graphics from the table.
meta.legend: How to read it: *(set by you)* marks the channel owner's own rules; the rest are learned from the references. Both are binding. "see vNN · title" names an example clip on the Nocturn board (productions/_boards/nocturn.json): v01 bodycam paranormal, v02 urban exploration, v03 psycho killers urbex, v04 forest encounters, v05 demon shopkeeper, v06 exploration encounters, v07 paranormal urbex, v08 YouTuber final moments, v09 body in cooler, v10 lost media, v11 streamer murdered, v12 live stream, v13 doorbell cam, v14 recorded final moments, v15 CCTV. "N of 15" counts the videos that show it. (est.) = judged by eye, not measured.
